subject: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@cobaltpay.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage

Elena / Ben —

Thanks for flagging the unexpected spike after the Apr 1 renewal. We pulled the usage and there is ~1.2M inference token-equivalent hours over the committed monthly capacity across the billing period. I attached a worksheet that breaks the hourly buckets and the per-unit pricing used for the invoice (CobaltPay_TrueUp_Worksheet.xlsx).

Quickly outlining options so we can move to agreement: 

1) One-time settlement: issue a one-time invoice for the overage amount ($28,000) and close the true-up.
2) Amortized top-up: spread the overage across the next 3 monthly invoices (approx. $9,500/month) to smooth cashflow.
3) Split approach: one-time smaller invoice + amortize remainder (if you need a partial payment).

If helpful, we can offer a retention credit as a gesture to cover part of the spike while you increase committed capacity (I’ll confirm with finance). Can you confirm which path you prefer and whether Procurement needs a PO first? If helpful, I’m free for a 30-min call today at 1pm PT.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0114

From: Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cobaltpay.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:43:21 -0700
Subject: Re: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick breakdown and for the worksheet. We ran an internal review and confirm the spike is real; it was driven by an unanticipated ML batch migration the week after renewals.

Procurement prefers amortization for cashflow reasons. Their questions: 
- Can the amortized plan be on our current Net30 terms?
- Can you provide a short amendment we can sign (we need language on the committed capacity increase once we finalize upsell)?

Ben (cc) is on billing and will provide the PO once we have the final amounts and the amendment. If you have a DocuSign link for the amendment + invoice schedule, send it over and we’ll route to signers.

Elena Morris
Head of Platform Ops | CobaltPay
elena@cobaltpay.com

Attachment: CobaltPay_usage_export_Apr2027.csv
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage

Team — looping you in. CobaltPay prefers amortization across 3 months on Net30. They’ll issue a PO after we provide amendment and final amounts.

Proposed finance-friendly structures (need signoff):
A) 3-month amortization: invoice three equal installments; include standard Net30 payment terms. No service interruption.
B) 1-month bridge + 2-month amortize: immediate invoice for 40% then two installments.
C) One-time invoice with 15% goodwill credit to incentivize immediate payment (we absorb as a retention credit).

Rough numbers from worksheet: gross overage = $28,000. If we consider a $5,000 retention credit (option C), net = $23,000. For amortization A => ~$9,333/mo.

Requesting: Laura — confirm accounting treatment and whether finance can accept amortized revenue over three invoices for recognition. Vivek — any commercial guidance on the $5k goodwill? Grace — customer success context if we push capacity upsell?

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:22:18 -0700
Subject: Re: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage

Jordan —

From an accounting perspective we can accommodate a 3-month amortization provided: 
- There is a signed amendment that explicitly states the overage settlement schedule and the amounts.
- We receive a PO referencing deal id DEAL-2027-0421 or the signed amendment prior to first invoice issuance.

Revenue recognition: we will recognize on a pro rata basis across invoices once invoices are issued. Please include the invoice numbering convention so AR can match payments to installments.

Other notes: Net30 terms are fine. For the one-time credit, finance needs approval from RevOps for any retention credits >$2,500 (to maintain margin thresholds). If Jordan confirms a $5k credit, we’ll route for quick clearance but expect additional review.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: True-up settlement & amortization options for renewal overage

Quick commercial note — given that CobaltPay is in-flight on a committed capacity upsell conversation, I recommend we approve a $5k retention credit (one-time) to keep momentum and lock additional committed capacity. We can frame it as a limited-time settlement credit conditioned on signing the amendment to raise committed capacity by 20% for the next 6 months.

If Laura needs a business case for RevOps, I can provide a short justification: projected net-new ARR from upsell > 10x the one-time credit and lowers future per-token unit costs (improves NRR).

Happy to sign off — Jordan, if you get procurement’s PO and Elena’s signature on the amendment, we can finalize and issue the first invoice.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cobaltpay.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltpay.com>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@cobaltpay.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Final: true-up settlement (agreed) + signed amendment and invoice schedule

Elena / Ben / Procurement —

Thanks for working through this. Per our conversation and approvals, here’s the agreed path: 

- Gross overage: $28,000
- Retention credit: $5,000 approved by Sales (Vivek) and RevOps pending final routing — net settled amount = $23,000
- Structure: 3-month amortization (3 invoices of $7,666.67 each) on Net30 terms
- Condition: CobaltPay signs the attached amendment committing to a 20% capacity increase for the next 6 months (amendment attached and DocuSign link below).

Attachments: Amendment_Signed_20270410.pdf (signed by CobaltPay; countersign pending), CobaltPay_TrueUp_Worksheet.xlsx
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Agreement-CPAY
HubSpot Deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2027-0421

Next steps for Procurement: please send PO referencing DEAL-2027-0421 and we’ll schedule the first invoice issue for May 1, 2027. AR will send invoice PDFs and payment instructions.

If any of you want to review the payment schedule on a call I’m available tomorrow morning. Appreciate the partnership here — looking forward to scaling capacity with you.

Best,
Jordan Blake
